cards.text: Friend, buckle up, because Judah is about to go through kings faster than I go through chocolate chips. The people of the land take Jehoahaz, son of Josiah, and make him king in Jerusalem in place of his father.

Jehoahaz is twenty-three when he becomes king, and he reigns in Jerusalem three MONTHS. Friend, that's not a reign, that's a FREE TRIAL, and it ends when the king of Egypt dethrones him and makes Judah pay a levy of silver and gold.

cards.question: The king of Egypt just dethroned Jehoahaz in Jerusalem. So who puts the next king on Judah's throne?

cards.text: Neco, king of Egypt, makes Eliakim, brother of Jehoahaz, king over Judah and Jerusalem. New crown AND a new name: Eliakim is now Jehoiakim.

cards.question: Neco, king of Egypt, isn't leaving Jehoahaz behind in Jerusalem. Where does Neco carry him off to?

cards.text: Jehoiakim is twenty-five when he becomes king, and he reigns in Jerusalem eleven years. After his brother's three months, ELEVEN YEARS is a lifetime achievement award!

cards.question: King Jehoiakim does what is right in the sight of the LORD his God.

cards.text: Then Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, comes up against Jehoiakim. He binds him with bronze shackles.

cards.question: Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, has Jehoiakim in bronze shackles. Where is he taking him?
Besides King Jehoiakim, what else does Nebuchadnezzar take from Jerusalem to Babylon?

answers.text: Some articles from the house of the LORD
Some stones from the wall of Jerusalem
Some gates from the city of Jerusalem

cards.text: Those articles from the house of the LORD? Nebuchadnezzar puts them in his temple in Babylon.
The rest of Jehoiakim's story, abominations and all, is written in the Book of the Kings of Israel and Judah. Then his son Jehoiachin reigns in his place.

cards.question: Jehoiachin is eighteen when he becomes king. Like his father Jehoiakim, he does evil in the sight of the LORD.
Jehoiachin is now king in Jerusalem. How long does he reign there?

cards.text: Three months and ten days, friend, and that's ten whole days longer than his uncle got! In the spring, Nebuchadnezzar summons Jehoiachin and brings him to Babylon, along with the articles of value from the house of the LORD.

cards.question: Jehoiachin is gone to Babylon, and Judah needs a new king. Who makes Jehoiachin's relative Zedekiah king over Judah and Jerusalem?

cards.text: Zedekiah is twenty-one when he becomes king, and he reigns in Jerusalem eleven years. He does evil in the sight of the LORD his God, and there's a prophet speaking for the LORD right there: Jeremiah.

cards.question: King Zedekiah humbles himself before Jeremiah the prophet.

cards.text: Here's the thing. King Nebuchadnezzar had made Zedekiah swear by God.

cards.question: Zedekiah swore by God to King Nebuchadnezzar. So what does Zedekiah do?

answers.text: He keeps his oath to him
He asks him for an army

cards.text: Zedekiah stiffens his neck and hardens his heart against turning to the LORD. Friend, that is NOT a posture problem.

The leaders of the priests and the people multiply their unfaithful deeds and defile the house of the LORD. And still, again and again, the LORD, the God of their fathers, sends word to His people through His messengers.

cards.question: Why does the LORD keep sending messengers to His people again and again?

answers.text: They asked Him for a sign

cards.question: The LORD keeps sending messengers because He has compassion on His people. How do the people treat those messengers?

answers.text: They mock and scoff at them

cards.text: They keep despising His words until the wrath of the LORD against His people is stirred up beyond remedy. So He brings up the king of the Chaldeans against them.

cards.question: God gives His people all into the hand of the king of the Chaldeans, ___.

cards.text: Young men are put to the sword in the sanctuary, sparing neither young nor old. Nebuchadnezzar carries off everything to Babylon, from the articles of the house of God to the treasures of the king and his officials.

cards.question: The Chaldeans set fire to the house of God.

cards.text: They break down the wall of Jerusalem and burn down all the palaces. Those who escaped the sword are carried off to Babylon to serve Nebuchadnezzar and his sons.

cards.question: The exiles stay servants to Nebuchadnezzar and his sons until the kingdom of ___ comes to power.
Back home, the land enjoys its Sabbath rest all the days of the desolation, until ___ years are completed, fulfilling the word of the LORD spoken through Jeremiah.

cards.text: Now it's the first year of Cyrus, king of Persia. And the word of the LORD spoken through Jeremiah is about to be fulfilled.

cards.question: Cyrus, king of Persia, sends a proclamation throughout his kingdom and puts it in writing. Who stirred his spirit to do it?
In his proclamation, Cyrus says the LORD, the God of heaven, has given him all the kingdoms of the earth. What does Cyrus say the LORD appointed him to do?

answers.text: Build Him a house at Jerusalem

cards.question: Cyrus tells anyone who belongs to the LORD's people that they may go up.

findings.problem: The question "Besides King Jehoiakim, what else does Nebuchadnezzar take from Jerusalem to Babylon?" says Jehoiakim was taken to Babylon. 2 Chronicles 36:6 only says Nebuchadnezzar bound him with bronze shackles "to take him to Babylon." It never says he was actually taken. The 36:7 phrasing "also took" refers to the articles, not to a completed deportation of Jehoiakim. Reword so it doesn't claim Jehoiakim arrived in Babylon. For example: "Nebuchadnezzar also takes something from the house of the LORD to Babylon. What is it?"

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates stop 1. It has 6 multiple choice cards (3, 5, 9, 10, 14, 16), 2 true or false cards (7, 13) and no fill in the blank cards. Swap in some fill in the blank cards, for example card 14 (the length of Jehoiachin's reign) or card 5 (where Neco carries Jehoahaz), so no one type wins by a wide margin.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: This card is the passage's big turn from seventy years of desolation to the first year of Cyrus, and it reads flat with no Papa Dorin voice. Stop 2's story cards are mostly plain retelling. Only card 5 carries a joke. The judgment and fall rightly stay sober, but the hopeful turn on card 16 can hold a real laugh or a storyteller's lift without muddying a fact.

rule.text: When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
